h.strategy: Borrow interaction patterns from other empirical sciences: epistasis in genetics (the effect of one mutation depends on genetic background, and beneficial mutations help fitter backgrounds less), diminishing returns in economics, and redundancy in engineered systems. Translate each pattern into a concrete conditional hypothesis about how an edit's effect varies with the parent configuration. Favor predictions that a practitioner thinking only mechanistically would get wrong, especially background-dependent sign changes and weaker gains in already-strong parents. Use conditions that many parents satisfy. In the flaw step, discard analogies that do not transfer and keep only those with a plausible general reason to hold.

hyps.why: Parallel 3x3 convs summed into the output node saturate, so a second conv adds less than when edge 5 is weak.
Diminishing returns at node 2: a 3x3 conv on edge 1 is partly redundant when edge 2 already supplies one.
A residual shortcut complements a strong deep path, and giving up edge 3's own op costs less when edge 5 already provides a conv.
Restoring the input-to-output residual from nothing yields a far larger gain than replacing an already-useful op on edge 3.
With edge 5 removed node 2 never reaches the output, so any edit on edge 2 has essentially zero effect.
A sibling 3x3 conv into node 2 buffers the information loss of a pool on edge 2.
When node 1 holds only pooled low-pass features, a learned 3x3 transform on edge 2 adds more than when node 1 is already conv-processed or empty.
When the upstream edge already provides spatial receptive field, a 1x1 conv on edge 5 is a near-substitute for a 3x3.
A 3x3 conv on edge 1 supplies spatial context to node 2, reducing the penalty of using only 1x1 on edge 5.
With edge 4 removed node 1 reaches the output only via the indirect edge 2 to edge 5 path, diluting or nullifying the value of a conv on edge 0.
